Funny Farm

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Funny farm. Don't be mislead by the name, this story is anything but funny.

Unique Selling Point:
Welcome to Funny farm. Sounds entertaining? On the contrary, it is a place that people refer to as the devil’s home. Nestled in the peaceful suburb of Alberton North, criminals squad illegally on government property from where crimes are planned and executed while authorities seemingly turn a blind eye.

Summary:
In April, Carlos Rheede was murdered in his apartment block in Rosettenville, South of Johannesburg. His murderers were traced to a place criminals know they will never get caught. A place where they get away with murder. Where people are killed and bodies hid under beds for weeks. a Place the police enter with caution. Funny farm, a white squatter camp in Alberton North, has become the breeding ground for crimes, a harbouring place for criminals and a drug den distributing across the greater South. Drugs are even sold to children in primary schools. Its a place where people turn a blind eye when mother sell their children for drug money. And the most ironic part of it all, the property was formerly used as a creche and teacher training college, belonging to the Gauteng Department of Education that has failed to move the squatters since 2014.

Further information:
Funny farm is a predominately white squatter camp in Alberton North. It has always been a place where homeless people could go for shelter. Churches and NGO's have always supplied food and clothes to the camp, but lately, that has not been necessary. Funny farm is called so because funny things started to happen a couple of years ago. Criminal networks were formed and residents started to participate in the planning and execution of crimes in the Alberton area. The criminals are mostly drug users and dealers and most crimes committed in the area are drug related. The police have raided the place numerous times since the start of 2022 but it does not solve the problem. The real problem lies with the owners of the property, the Gauteng Department of Education. But once again, the buck is passed between officials as no one wants to take responsibility. The Gauteng department of Infrastructure has escalated the problem to the HOD of GDE already in 2014 but nothing was done. Now, the problem has grown. The squatter camp is expanding and lawlessness is at the order of the day.

Reason for legal: We are holding the department of Education accountable for allowing criminal squatters on their property and doing nothing to move them.
If residents or criminals tell us on camera that the Alberton Police are involved in criminalities in Funny farm, we will also have to approach them with the info.

Script:


FUNNY FARM

VO
In late April, the owner of this block of flats in Rosettenville, in central Johannesburg, was murdered here. After his burnt remains were found in a park behind his house, his killers were traced to Alberton, South of the city, to an informal settlement in the middle of a residential suburb.

NEW VO
Notorious for criminal activity, the killers may have thought they’d find cover here, but they were chased out, and later arrested in a deserted house down the road.

The people in the settlement don’t want to attract unnecessary police attention because – well - funny things happen in this place. That’s how it got its name: Funny Farm (pause) and why they call themselves farmers.

VO
In the crevices, behind curtains, wood and scrap metal, families live amongst felons, drug dealers, thieves, and rapists. Only about a 130 people live here in an area the size of two street blocks

VO
We are told to watch our step, so we get back-up before going in. The farmers don’t want us here.

VO
Hiding from our cameras, they insist we’re trespassing on private property – but we know differently. These buildings are hijacked, the land around them illegally occupied.

PTC
It is actually difficult to describe to anyone what it is that we saw there. It is, you can’t understand how people can live like this. There are different families in small little rooms, and it is dirty, and it smells, and it is totally inhospitable, like I can’t even fathom what it must be like living day to day in a place like this.

VO
But, beneath this severe poverty lurks a sinister secret. Charities and churches deliver food and clothes to the camp, only for it to be sold on. Many of the squatters sell anything they can lay their hands on… part of a criminal network, operating in Alberton and the greater South of Johannesburg.

VO
Karen is of them. A self-professed criminal, she has been a farmer for over three years and agreed to talk to us if we kept her identity secret.

PTC
So, we had to pick up Karen and take her to a remote location because if we interview her anywhere near Funny Farm, we might just put her life in danger.

SUPER@ “KAREN”
“There is different groups for different things. Hijacking, cables, you know, electrical cables, housebreaking”

VO
She tells us, most farmers sleep during the day but when night comes, they hit the streets.

SUPER@KAREN NO SUPER
“At ten o clock the first group goes out. They go check for cameras in the hood. Usually, a team leader he decides what area will be hit that night …there is always a team one. If they mess up, everybody gets locked up…The second group always have two people that’s got the knowledge for electricity and cameras…The third group is the ones that take the stolen goods and sell it”.

VO
They steal anything they can find, making life unbearable for Alberton’s residents.

SUPER@MALINDA BEUKES
“Break-ins, weather its residential houses, companies”

VO
Malinda Beukes lives down the road from Funny Farm.

SUPER@MALINDA BEUKES
“I mean, you leave your car in your driveway, and they come and steal all four mag wheels and leave it on bricks. Break into your car and steal tablets and laptops. Breaking into the houses, stealing of cars, it just goes on and on and on”

VO
Malinda has been hitting brick walls trying to bring the issue to the attention of the authorities. Finally, she contacted us to help expose what happens in the camp.

SUPER@MALINDA BEUKES
“It is affecting everybody and like I say it is not just Alberton it is extending to Alberton North or whatever to all the areas. So the people are all, they are just sick and tired of this because nothing gets done”

VO
Malinda used to help the children in the camp, but since drug dealers took control around two years ago, it’s become too dangerous.

SUPER@MALINDA BEUKES
“There was a caravan park in Alberton North in the industrial area where people were living in caravans. Really families that were struggling and it was never a problem. So when that place was sold, They moved over to where they are now …It was still fine, until people moved in that started the drug dealing and who knows what else”

VO
The drug dealers force the residents to pay rent.

SUPER@ KAREN
“The room I’m staying in, I did not even have a choice. They just decide, ok, you stay there. They split you up if they want to, if you’re a family they split you up. I ended up in one of the drug dealers rooms, right next to him and he wants me to either have to pay with sex or I have to pay R250 a week, and it is not that you have a choice.

VO
The drug dealers sublet property that does not belong to them//, The rightful owner of this land is the Gauteng Department of Education.

LINK
This building here on the left and the one on the right, belongs to the department of education, it used to be an old education center. But as you can see, for many years it hasn’t been used for the purpose that it was built for.

VO
Throughout our investigation, we reached out to the Department several times, but they insisted on dodging our questions. And every time we returned to the camp, we uncovered more shocking stories.

SUPER@ KAREN NO SUPER
“There is a lot of innocent people there that’s there that is doing things that they don’t want to do. You get…so you do petty crime and everything gets handed to this drug dealers and from there they decide who gets what… sometimes you don’t get anything at all”

VO
And the dealers have buyers for all the stolen goods. But Funny farm is also a one stop shop for drug addicts traveling from far and wide. Others have more expensive and sinister tastes.

SUPER@ KAREN
“There is a market for anything, from a vehicle to a child, it’s like a thru”

VO
Many tell us how children are sold in the camp. Sometimes by their own mothers.

VO
We meet two little girls who used to live in the camp. Now housed in safety, they tell us how they witnessed a neighbor sell her own children.

FILE: MIA AND ANGELIQUE
Sy het baie meer kinders gehad, maar hulle almal is verkoop. Om bier te koop. Ons weet nie vir wie nie. Net om bier te koop. Daar was 16 jaar kinders, sy het so baie kinders al gehad”
TRANSLATION AND SUBTITLE
She used to have many kids but all of them have been sold so she could buy beer. We don’t know to whom she sold them, but it was to buy beer. There were 16-year-olds… she had so many children.

SUPER@ KAREN NO SUPER
“Some of the girls, when they fall pregnant, and I always wonder what happened to the baby. Because the mother is so bad on drugs, on meth. Then you get this Samaritan that stops there with a Mercedes and offers them money for this baby and then just sells the baby as if it is nothing”.

VO
Local welfare says Funny farm is a dangerous place for children but that it’s not easy to remove them from their families.

SUPER@ZEENITH DOMINGO
“We have removed eight families children up to now. And the last three years that I have been here. It all relates to drugs. Abusive drugs, both parents on, using whilst pregnant, the mother, children at risk having withdrawal symptoms”.

VO
She says they are aware of children being sold, but that it is very hard to intervene.

MAC: DO YOU HAVE AN IDEA OF HOW MUCH THESE KIDS ARE BEIGN BOUGHT FOR?
SUPER@ZEENITH DOMINGO
“You know there is an attorney that is based here in Alberton, and she works with children’s matters. She said it was a hundred and forty some thousand”.

VO
Like welfare, the police are also aware of the goings on inside funny farm - teaming up with private tactical teams, they often raid the camp. Today’s operation – which they’ve let us film – has gunrunners in its sights. It’s no secret illegal weapons are hidden here – just another reason the criminal element doesn’t want to attract unnecessary attention. Within hours of a tip-off, police and other personnel swoop on the camp.

UPSOUND OF RAID

VO
One more illegal weapon is discovered, the rest seem to be fake guns used for hijackings and robberies.

VO
The drug dealing kingpins have a head start. They escape long before the police enter because surveillance cameras are set up across the camp. Even in this stall at the entrance where more than just fruit and veg are sold.

VO
The main kingpin lives here at the back of the camp. When police enter his private quarters, he has long gone.
UPSOUD- WHERE IS PAUL?

VO
Monitors for the cameras across the camp are set up in his room, his wife keeping a watchful eye on things

VO
Even if the police perform regular raids such as this one, they’re not a long-term solution. The rightful landowner must step in and close the gates, nearby residents say.

SUPER@MALINDA BEUKES
“That place needs to be closed down, and a proper shelter for homeless people should be built.”

VO
The Gauteng department of education or GDE is the only authority that can act, but – denying any responsibility – it says the buildings fall under the control of the department of infrastructure and development. But the GDE never signed off this Alberton property as a closed or gazetted school. And while the buck is being passed, there’s little hope for people like Karen.

REVERSAL MAC
DO YOU HAVE ANY OTHER CHOICE OUT OF YOUR SITUATION? IS THERE NO WAY OUT OF THIS?
KAREN
“I guess there is. I have been doing domestic and any kind of work I can do. But as soon as they hear I am from Funny farm, the job is finished they don’t have a job anymore. So, it is impossible to get back on your feet if you can’t get an income ”.

PROMOS
11”
In the northern parts of Alberton South of Johannesburg, unsettling things happen in a place called funny farm, but all is not in a name, because this story is everything but a joke.

21”
In an informal settlement outside Johannesburg, destitute people are forced into crime for survival, they work together to break into houses, cars and businesses to steal anything they can lay their hands on.

21”
Funny Farm, this is an informal settlement with a difference where destitute people work together as criminals living and dealing on a state owned property
